Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia Patel: okay everyone, uh—thanks for making time. I'm Sofia from Redwood, AE on the northwest region. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Daniel Ruiz: hey Sofia, Daniel here — Head of Alliances at NimbleEdge. Emma and Liam on my side as well.
[00:17] Emma Zhang: hi hi, Emma. Got a few notes.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: Marcus from Redwood, se — I'll handle the technical bits today.
[00:24] Priya Nair: Priya from Partnerships, quick intros and then straight into pipeline.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Liam, solutions architect, cheers.
[00:32] Sofia Patel: Awesome. Goal for today: pick five target accounts for a Q2 co-sell push, clarify revenue split and roles, and surface any technical blockers for the MediServe and ACME Retail prospects. Does that sound right?
[00:45] Daniel Ruiz: Yep, that's the agenda. NimbleEdge has these two warm opps — MediServe (healthcare) and ACME Retail — plus a couple of enterprise target accounts we'd like to joint-approach.
[00:53] Emma Zhang: quick bit: our sales cycles for healthcare are a bit longer because of security, data residency. We'll need SOC2 type certs and an option for private deployment.
[01:04] Marcus Lee: that's expected — Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem footprints and we have KMS hooks; I'll follow up with a network diagram and list of controls.
[01:12] Liam O'Connor: great, Marcus. For MediServe specifically we need to see egress rules and if KV-cache persists on disk — we have to show no PHI leaves the VPC.
[01:22] Marcus Lee: yeah, there's some nuance — the KV cache is in-memory by default but persists to checkpointing on Dedicated deployments; we can turn off persistent logs. (mic garble) we should doc that.
[01:36] Sofia Patel: ok, back to pipeline: Daniel, can you run through the top 6 accounts you think are priority and why?
[01:42] Daniel Ruiz: sure. First — MediServe, very strong champion, budget in hand but must be VPC/private. Second — ACME Retail, big skus, latency sensitive, want sub-50ms for product search. Third — Orion Financial, compliance heavy but big ARR. Fourth — Hargen Logistics — mostly cost-driven. Fifth — BlueWave Media — more experimental, could be a hosted-first use. Sixth is a stretch, DataWorks, but they might move quick.
[02:12] Emma Zhang: to add: ACME is sensitive to inference latency and cost; they'd prefer on-prem but open to dedicated in-cloud if latency's consistent.
[02:21] Sofia Patel: good. For go-to-market roles: NimbleEdge handles first-touch and qualification, we jump in with SE-led demo + benchmark, then joint contract. Revenue split question: Priya, do you want to outline a standard partner discount or do we negotiate per-deal?
[02:36] Priya Nair: I'd prefer a framework: baseline partner discount of 20% on hosted list + additional margin for referrals that bring net-new accounts. For Dedicated/reserved it's different — we should propose a fixed uplift to cover committed capacity. We'll send a draft.
[02:49] Daniel Ruiz: 20% baseline seems fair. But we need clarity on who owns renewals and how pipeline is tracked.
[02:56] Sofia Patel: we can track in the shared pipeline sheet (I'll create) and define ownership per-opportunity. Typically Redwood maintains billing but partners get credited for the sale for the first 12 months; renewals can be negotiated.
[03:10] Emma Zhang: call that out in the one-pager so our reps know.
[03:14] Sofia Patel: will do.
[03:16] Marcus Lee: switching to tech: ACME's latency requirement — sub-50ms tail for product search. That's probably only achievable with edge-optimized Dedicated instances or on-prem inference. Hosted shared endpoints will be a stretch unless we do heavy quantization and aggressive caching.
[03:35] Liam O'Connor: can you quantify "stretch" — are we talking 80-120ms?
[03:39] Marcus Lee: roughly. On standard hosted, in our benchmarks with similar model sizes we see 70–150ms depending on traffic and burst. With Dedicated and tuned batching/cache we can hit 30–50ms tail in many cases.
[03:50] Daniel Ruiz: That's helpful. For ACME a demo showing Dedicated hitting the SLA will be critical — otherwise we lose them to on-prem vendors.
[03:58] Sofia Patel: noted — Marcus to prepare a short benchmarking note and a canned demo configuration.
[04:05] Marcus Lee: yep. I'll include a config for autoscaling, burst pools, and kernel selection notes.
[04:12] Emma Zhang: on the legal/compliance side — what docs do you have for SOC2 and data residency? We need an SOC2 report and logs for audits.
[04:20] Sofia Patel: we have SOC2 Type II reports and a security pack; I'll attach links in the follow-up. Also, Redwood Console exposes audit logs and token-level tracing for requests.
[04:31] Liam O'Connor: can you share an example of the audit log output? We need to show auditors a sample.
[04:36] Sofia Patel: yes, I'll include a sanitized sample.
[04:38] (background noise)
[04:42] Daniel Ruiz: quick question on pricing: do you have partner pricing for pilots vs production? ACME will need a pilot price to get through procurement.
[04:50] Priya Nair: we usually do a time-limited pilot discount. For hosted pilots we can do 40% off list for 3 months; for Dedicated we can provide a trial commitment credit with a conversion path.
[05:02] Sofia Patel: I'll capture that in the one-pager and pipeline sheet.
[05:06] Emma Zhang: perfect. For MediServe, data residency is a blocker — they require logs not stored outside EU. We need to ensure that with your private option, logs remain in-customer VPC.
[05:17] Marcus Lee: we can deploy Redwood Private in their region — logs can be configured to route to customer-managed storage. I'll follow up with a network/topology doc.
[05:26] Liam O'Connor: also, small nit — is there a way to turn off telemetry for PII-sensitive requests?
[05:30] Marcus Lee: yes, PII filtering and telemetry controls are configurable; again we'll include specifics.
[05:35] Sofia Patel: great.
[05:37] [00:05:40] (00:05:40 timestamp alignment note — small audio glitch)
[05:40] Daniel Ruiz: on go-to-market, can we run a joint webinar targeted at retail and healthcare? NimbleEdge has a mailing list and a monthly webinar slot. We could slot Redwood for May.
[05:50] Priya Nair: a webinar is a good demand gen play. We should build a joint case study or demo — maybe focus on low-latency search for ACME and secure PII handling for MediServe.
[06:04] Sofia Patel: yes — action: build two short demo flows and a joint landing page. I'll draft copy.
[06:10] Emma Zhang: who will own the invite list? NimbleEdge can provide the audience; Redwood can provide email copy.
[06:16] Sofia Patel: NimbleEdge to own outreach, Redwood to approve assets.
[06:20] [00:06:24] (short pause)
[06:29] Marcus Lee: quick technical ops question: for Dedicated — what's the typical lead time for capacity provisioning? Our customers ask that a lot.
[06:36] Sofia Patel: depends on GPU type and region — typical baseline pool provisioning is 2–4 weeks; for priority/enterprise customers we can expedite with committed contracts.
[06:45] Daniel Ruiz: that timeline affects ACME's procurement — they want production in 8 weeks. If provisioning is 2–4 weeks and integration is 4–6 that's tight but doable.
[06:56] Sofia Patel: we'll map a project plan in the follow-up so procurement has clear milestones.
[07:02] Emma Zhang: one more: attribution and leads — NimbleEdge wants co-sell credit even if they hand off a net-new opportunity to Redwood. How do you handle partner-sourced deals?
[07:12] Priya Nair: partner-sourced leads are tracked in the partner portal and we have a 90–120 day credit window. We'll confirm exact window in the doc.
[07:22] Daniel Ruiz: okay, that's workable.
[07:25] [00:07:30] (someone coughs)
[07:31] Sofia Patel: jumping ahead — next steps recap: I'll send one-pager, joint deck, and pipeline sheet. Marcus will send network/topology + latency benchmarking note. Daniel will confirm 5 target accounts and champions. Priya will share draft revenue-split. Anything else?
[07:48] Liam O'Connor: Marcus, can you also include a short checklist for auditors — SOC2 artifacts, SSO/SAML config, KMS integration notes?
[07:58] Marcus Lee: absolutely.
[08:01] Emma Zhang: please also include estimated monthly unit costs for the ACME configuration so procurement can budget.
[08:08] Sofia Patel: will include cost scenarios (hosted vs dedicated vs private) with example token throughput pricing.
[08:15] Daniel Ruiz: cool. Also can we surface competitor differentiation? We fight Anthropic a bit, and Databricks on model hosting sometimes.
[08:24] Sofia Patel: yes — I'll include a short competitive snip highlighting performance / cost / unified ops.
[08:30] [00:08:35] (transcription hiccup)
[08:36] Daniel Ruiz: last administrative thing — can we get an intro to your partner success rep? They handle the onboarding?
[08:42] Priya Nair: that's me for now, but we'll loop in partner success once we have the first pilot signed.
[08:49] Sofia Patel: great. Any final Qs?
[08:52] Emma Zhang: none from me.
[08:53] Liam O'Connor: no, thanks.
[08:55] Marcus Lee: all good. I'll follow up with the tech docs.
[08:58] Sofia Patel: thanks everyone, we'll send the follow-up with links — Google Drive deck: https://drive.google.com/example-redwood-nimbleedge (sanitized). Also pipeline spreadsheet link will be shared.
[09:10] Daniel Ruiz: thanks folks, talk soon.
[09:13] Sofia Patel: bye.

Meeting end.
